data.name: Smitansh
data.gender_notes: Smitansh is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from Sanskrit 'smita' (grace, pleasure) and 'ansh' (part, portion). It signifies the grace of a deity or the divine presence bestowed upon an individual. The name Smitansh carries the meaning “God's grace” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Smitansh usually hope their child will grow to embody god's grace and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name blessed by the divine, carrying the grace and blessings of the gods.
data.etymology: Smitansh belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God's grace.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Smitansh total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: The name Smitansh has deep roots in Indian culture. In Hindu mythology, a smita is a graceful smile or expression that embodies the divine love and compassion of various gods and goddesses. Using this expression as the root of the name adds an element of grace and charm to the individual name. In addition, the use of Sanskrit words signifies a connection to traditional Indian culture and language.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Smitansh reflects the spiritual belief in the influence and presence of the divine in everyday life. The name can be interpreted as a reminder of the grace and blessings of the gods and goddesses in Hindu religion. By carrying this name, an individual is believed to invite the blessings and protection of the divine beings, enhancing their spiritual growth and inner peace.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Smitansh symbolizes the deep inner joy and contentment that arises from the realization of one's true self. The prefix 'Smita' means joy or happiness, and 'Ansh' refers to the divine essence within us. Thus, Smitansh signifies the everlasting happiness that comes from connecting with one's inner self and the divine.

vedic_reference.note: This name is derived from the Sanskrit words स्मित: (smita) which means a smile and अन्ष: (ansh) which means appearance or manifestation. It is not directly related to any Vedic text or mythology.
